html:
Added

  • Admin — importing members now checks the whole file first, brings across time-credit balances and towns, and imports in timed batches with a progress screen. Nothing is imported until the entire file passes: if any row has a problem the import stops, nothing is created, and every problem is listed in plain words by spreadsheet row and column, with the list downloadable. A wrong file (an Excel workbook, a file that is not UTF-8, tab-separated, an old template, missing, extra or empty columns, or headings not on the first line) is refused with a pop-up and a "Download the correct template" button. Semicolon-separated files and decimal commas from European Excel are accepted, and the apostrophe the platform's own export puts in front of values that start with =, +, - or @ is undone. The template has first_name, last_name, email, phone, location (the member's town, optional) and balance (optional), with headings only and no example rows. A balance is carried over as an opening balance wallet entry (new transaction type opening_balance, sender 0) that the member sees as "Opening balance carried over from your previous timebank" (the import reference is stored on the entry and shown to the admin on the results screen); the most that can be carried over is 100,000 hours, a negative balance starts at 0 with the original recorded and listed in the results, and an imported member never also receives welcome credits (including when an admin approves them later). The import runs in batches the browser paces itself (10 to 200 rows, each stopped by the server after about 8 seconds), with a progress screen showing the bar, "batch n of about m", counts, hours and time left; it cannot be closed mid-run, can be stopped after the current batch, never duplicates a batch that is sent twice, and finishes an interrupted import. The results list balances set to zero, members whose identity step did not complete, and rows not imported (downloadable). Limits and safeguards: a fresh second-factor confirmation (step-up) is needed for the check and every batch, admins only, 2 MB and 5,000 rows per file, one held import per admin, the check is limited to 10 a minute per admin, and the member data the server holds for a checked file is discarded as soon as the import completes or is stopped (pressing Stop tells the server, through stop: true on the batch endpoint); otherwise it expires within two hours, for example when the connection is lost mid-import. Each imported member gets a member_imported audit entry, the completed import gets member_import_completed, and the activity-feed entry is kept. Results are announced to screen readers, focus moves to them, and progress is announced every 10%. New routes: POST /v2/admin/members/import/check, POST /v2/admin/members/import/{importId}/batch and GET /v2/admin/members/import/template. The import window also offers, ticked by default, to email each new member a link to set their password: one invitation per created member is queued in the same database transaction as the member (members held for an identity check are not emailed and can be invited from the member list once approved), the emails go out in the background at about one a second, the window gives the estimate before and after, and the batch endpoint takes send_invitations on the first batch only. Not part of this change: exporting a file ready to re-import, and asking members for their town at onboarding.

  • Admin — an administrator can mark a member's email as confirmed. On Admin → Users → a member, the Email activation card now has "Mark as confirmed" beside "Resend verification email", after an "are you sure?" step that names the address. It unblocks a member who is stuck at sign-in because a community requires email confirmation. It applies exactly the same rule as the member clicking their own verification link (so on a self-serve community the account is also activated, and on a community that screens new members only an already-approved one is), is recorded in the activity and audit logs, and never releases an identity-check hold. Admins who outrank the member only; brokers are refused. Sent as email_verified: true on the existing PUT /v2/admin/users/{id}; there is no "unconfirm".

  • Volunteering — organisations can remove an approved volunteer, and the people who run an organisation can no longer volunteer for it (website, accessible site and server). An organisation's owner and its team owners/admins can now take an approved volunteer off one of its opportunities: on the website from the organisation dashboard's Applications tab and from the applicants panel on the opportunity page, and on the accessible site from the organisation's Manage page, each after an "are you sure?" step. The volunteer is told, any shift place is offered to the waiting list, the removal is recorded in the organisation's audit log, and they can apply again later. This also lets someone remove their own old application. Until now only the person who created an opportunity was stopped from applying to it; anyone else who runs the organisation could apply, and then nobody could decide the application because nobody decides their own. Now the opportunity page shows them a short "you run this organisation" note with a link to manage its applications instead of an Apply button, and the server refuses the application with a plain message (shown as such on the accessible site). Community admins are not affected unless they run the organisation. People who run an organisation can still log hours and claim expenses with it; another admin decides those (owner decision, keeping the 2 Oct design). On the accessible site a refused expense claim now shows the server's own reason instead of a generic failure. New endpoint POST /v2/volunteering/applications/{id}/remove; GET /v2/volunteering/opportunities/{id} now returns runs_organisation. Group sign-ups (switched off everywhere) can still add someone who runs the organisation to a shift.

  • Volunteering — admins can remove an approved volunteer from an opportunity. Until now nothing anywhere let an admin take a volunteer off an opportunity once their application was approved. On Admin → Volunteering → Applications an approved row's menu now has "Remove from opportunity"; after an "are you sure?" step the volunteer's place is ended, they are told by bell and phone notification in their own language, the removal is recorded in the organisation's audit log (who removed whom, from which opportunity), and a place they held on a shift that has not started is offered to the next person on its waiting list. They can apply again later. A pending application is still declined rather than removed. New endpoint POST /v2/admin/volunteering/approvals/{id}/remove (admins only; refuses anything but an approved application with 422, and another community's with 404).

  • Volunteering — group sign-ups now work the way the wording promised (website, server and admin; still switched off everywhere until a community admin opts in). A group leader who reserves places on a shift and names a member now creates a real sign-up for that member: the member appears in My shifts, can check in, is told by bell and email in their own language that the leader signed them up, and can take themselves off the shift. Removing a member or cancelling the booking tells the people affected straight away rather than waiting for a digest. A named member's place is counted once, through the group's reserved places, so a shift no longer reads as full twice over. On the website the Group sign-ups tab lets a leader remove a member or cancel the whole booking and lets a member leave, each after an "are you sure?" step, and no longer shows a Pending or Declined state that could never happen. Admins get a new page, Admin → Volunteering → Group bookings, listing every booking in the community with search and a status filter kept in the address, and can cancel one, which releases its places and every member's sign-up and tells the group (GET /v2/admin/volunteering/group-reservations, DELETE …/group-reservations/{id}). New notification types vol_group_signup_added, vol_group_signup_removed, vol_group_signup_cancelled are sent immediately (gaps A8, C7).

  • Phone app — organisers can now run their shifts, expenses and fundraising from the phone (needs an app release). Until now the app could only show shifts to volunteers; nothing on a phone could create, change or remove one. From the organisation dashboard an organiser can now: see every opportunity the organisation has posted, including closed and cancelled ones; add, change or remove a one-off shift and set up repeating weekly or fortnightly shifts, with the same rules and the same server refusals as the website; open a shift's roster to see who is signed up, who is on the waiting list, who came from a group booking and who has checked in; review volunteer expense claims (approve, reject with a reason, mark as paid, never on their own claim); and run fundraising campaigns, confirm hand-overs and see gifts and history, as on the website. An opportunity can now be deleted from the phone, after confirmation. New translation namespace volunteeringOrganiser in all seven app languages (gap M2).

  • Phone app — volunteers get the rest of their tools (needs an app release). A new My tools list on the volunteering screen opens, each only where the community has it switched on: waiting lists (a full shift now offers Join waiting list instead of a sign-up the server refuses, shows the member's position, and lets them leave or claim a freed place); wellbeing check-ins with the same "Let someone get in touch with me" choice as the website; urgent shift requests to accept or decline; the qualifications register (a record, never an upload); accessibility needs (a private note); group sign-ups (alpha, off unless the community opted in); the member's own check-in code as a QR code and as text; and reporting a safeguarding concern with the same form and the plain-English status of earlier reports. Expense claims can carry a receipt photo from the phone, and giving by card opens the website in the browser. New translation namespace volunteeringVolunteer in all seven app languages (gap M3).

  • Accessible site — group sign-ups can now be used end to end (only where a community has switched the feature on). Group leaders can reserve places on a volunteer shift for their group, choosing the opportunity, shift, group and number of places on ordinary web pages. Adding someone works by searching their name and choosing them, instead of typing a member number that was shown nowhere. Each reservation shows its members; removing a member or cancelling asks "are you sure?" first, with no JavaScript needed. The wording now says what really happens: a member you add is signed up to the shift, told about it, and can take themselves off it. The feature stays switched off on every community until an admin turns it on.

  • Volunteering — a volunteer who says they are struggling is now heard. Until now a wellbeing check-in was saved and shown back to the volunteer, and used for nothing else: the wellbeing score looked only at shifts and logged hours, and nobody was ever told (on hOUR Timebank six "Struggling" check-ins in three days left the score at 80 and raised no alert). Now a Low or Struggling check-in in the last 14 days lowers the score (Struggling alone gives "high" risk) and shows a warning, and a later better check-in clears it. When a volunteer chooses Low or Struggling, the check-in form (website and accessible site) asks "Let someone get in touch with me", ticked by default and explained in plain words; if they leave it ticked, a wellbeing alert is raised and the community's safeguarding staff (admins, brokers, coordinators) and the owners, admins and liaison people of every organisation they volunteered with in the last 180 days get a bell notification and an email in their own language. Staff can read the volunteer's note after signing in; it is never put in an email, and organisations are told the name and how the volunteer feels, never the note. Nobody is told about themselves, and people are told at most once a day per volunteer. A client that does not send the choice shares nothing. Brokers and coordinators can now list and act on wellbeing alerts (GET/PUT /v2/admin/volunteering/wellbeing/alerts moved to the broker-or-admin group), which now carry reason and latest_checkin, and the alerts panel also appears on the broker volunteering safeguarding page. POST /v2/volunteering/wellbeing/checkin accepts share_with_team and returns shared and team_notified; recent check-ins carry shared. New columns vol_mood_checkins.share_with_team and team_notified_at (appended; instant). The accessible wellbeing page no longer says "Only you can see this" without qualification.

  • Accessible site — volunteers can record their own qualifications; document uploads are gone. The owner decided that qualifications are recorded, never uploaded, and the website switched to a no-upload register on 5 Oct. The accessible site now has the same register at /volunteering/qualifications: list (grouped as needs attention, awaiting confirmation, confirmed, withdrawn), add, edit (with a warning that editing a confirmed record clears its confirmation), and withdraw with a reason, in the website's own wording in all 11 languages. It is listed on the volunteering page and qualification reminders (?tab=credentials) now open it. The old document-upload page /volunteering/credentials forwards to the register (its old form posts do nothing but forward), its download address is gone, and the upload endpoint POST /v2/volunteering/credentials has been removed from the API (no client used it any more). Documents uploaded before today can still be listed, downloaded and deleted through the API; nothing stored was deleted (gap B15).

  • Volunteering — an organisation's team can now be managed. Until now nobody could add or remove a volunteer organisation's members or change their roles after it was created. Community admins (Admin → Volunteering → Organisations → Members) and the organisation's owners (new Team tab on the organisation dashboard, and a Team page on the accessible site) can add someone from the community as owner, admin or member, change a role, or remove someone; the organisation's admins can see the team but not change it. Safeguards are enforced by the server: the person who registered the organisation and your own place cannot be changed, the last owner cannot be removed, and only active members of the same community can be added. Each change is recorded in the organisation audit log and the person is told in their own language. New routes: GET/POST /v2/volunteering/organisations/{id}/members, PUT/DELETE …/members/{memberId}, and the same writes under /v2/admin/volunteering/organizations/{id}/members (gap D7).

  • Volunteering — admins can see and revoke volunteer certificates. A new admin page (Volunteering → Certificates) lists every certificate issued in the community, with search by name, email or code, and lets staff download the printable copy (without marking it downloaded) or revoke one issued in error with a recorded reason. A revoked certificate fails the public check exactly as an unknown code does, its printable copy is refused, the holder is told in their own language, and the website and accessible site both show it as revoked with no download. New nullable columns vol_certificates.revoked_at, revoked_by, revoke_reason (appended; instant). Guessed admin addresses such as /admin/volunteering/applications, /incidents, /settings, /organisations, /fundraising, /shift-swaps, /shifts and /wellbeing now redirect to the real page instead of "page not found". check:db-columns now also recognises columns added by Schema::table migrations (gap D8).

  • Admin → Volunteering → Expenses: admins can now add an expense policy for an expense type that has none (maximum per claim, monthly maximum, receipt threshold, whether approval is needed). Until now a community with no policies saw "No expense policies configured" and had no way to create one: the API could only update a policy that already existed. Blank limits mean "no limit". An organisation from another community is refused.

  • Volunteering → My Hours (website): members can now see each hour entry they have logged, with its date, where it was for and whether it is waiting, approved or declined, and the shifts they hold, upcoming and past, each linking to its opportunity. Until now the tab showed only totals. Both lists load ten at a time with Load more. Entries cannot be changed or withdrawn from here, because the platform has no way to do that once logged.

  • Volunteering → My expenses (accessible site): a volunteer can attach a receipt to an expense claim (PDF, JPG, PNG or WebP, up to 10 MB), as on the website. A file of the wrong type or over 10 MB is refused with a message beside the field, and nothing is sent. A claim without a receipt is sent exactly as before. Website: the expense form's "Receipt" label was still in English in eight languages and is now translated.

  • Volunteering → certificates: anyone holding a volunteer's certificate (an employer, a college) can now check it is genuine without an account, at /verify-certificate on the community's website. They enter the code printed on the certificate and the volunteer's name as printed. They are told only whether the two match and, if they do, the details already on the certificate: hours, period, organisations and issue date. A wrong name gets exactly the same answer as a code that does not exist, so a code on its own reveals nothing about who holds it, and the check is limited to 20 tries a minute per network address. Names match regardless of capital letters, spacing and accents. The printed certificate now gives the page's address, and the Verify button on a volunteer's certificate opens it. New public route POST /v2/volunteering/certificates/check (code, name); the signed-in GET /v2/volunteering/certificates/verify/{code} is unchanged and still refuses anonymous callers. Owner decision, 6 Oct 2026: a narrow exception to the July rule that certificate lookups need a sign-in, because it confirms only what the person already holds.

  • Volunteering → certificates (accessible site): the same certificate check now exists on the accessible site, at /verify-certificate on every community's accessible address, built with the standard GOV.UK form, error summary and notification banner. A code in the address only fills in the box; nothing is looked up until a name is entered, and the name is sent in the form body, never in the address. A community with volunteering switched off answers "page not found". Each certificate on a volunteer's Volunteer certificates page now has a Check this certificate link to it, with the code filled in. New strings in all eleven languages (govuk_alpha_volunteering.certificate_check.*).

  • Volunteering → an opportunity's page (accessible site): the people who run an opportunity can now change its details, close it to new volunteers, reopen it, and cancel it, as they can on the website since 6 Oct 2026. Before this, an opportunity posted on the accessible site could never be changed or withdrawn there. Edit opens the posting form filled in (the organisation is shown, not asked; a changed place drops the old map pin), with field-by-field error messages. Cancelling goes through a confirmation page that warns it cannot be undone, says approved volunteers will be told, and offers closing instead. The page shows Closed to new volunteers or Cancelled, volunteers can no longer apply to either, and a cancelled opportunity offers nothing more to change. Posting an opportunity now ends on its page with "Your opportunity has been posted. Add shifts so volunteers can sign up." — the confirmation the create form had always asked for but the page never showed. New strings in all eleven languages (govuk_alpha_volunteering.opp_manage.*).

  • Volunteering → an opportunity's page (accessible site): a volunteer who holds an upcoming shift now sees Check in at your shift, with the same QR code the website and phone app show, whether they have checked in yet, and when they arrived and left. Until now the accessible site had no check-in at all. The QR is drawn on the server, so it works without JavaScript; it encodes the same check-in address as the other clients, so whoever scans it lands on one confirmation page. A community with QR check-in switched off shows nothing. The venue member pass now draws its QR with the same shared helper, which also stops an XML declaration being written into the middle of the page.

  • Volunteering → organisation dashboard (accessible site): Expense claims, where an organisation's owner and administrators review the expense claims its volunteers have made. A volunteer could already claim an expense on the accessible site, but the organisation had nowhere there to see the claim. The page shows claims waiting for review by default, with tabs for approved, paid, rejected and all; the organisation's totals; and, on each claim, only the next step that is allowed: Approve or Reject (with an optional reason) for a waiting claim, Mark as paid (with an optional payment reference) for an approved one. A reviewer's own claim offers no action, only a note that another administrator must review it. Receipts download and are never opened inside the site. The totals always cover every claim; the website's Expenses tab shows totals for the current filter only (so "Approved" reads 0 on its Pending view), which is unchanged. New strings in all eleven languages (govuk_alpha_volunteering.org_expenses.*); :name — :amount is added to scripts/php-lang-invariant-allowlist.json because it has nothing to translate.

  • Volunteering → organisation dashboard (accessible site): Fundraising, where an organisation's owner and administrators run campaigns for their own organisation, as on the website since 5 Oct 2026. Until now the accessible site had no fundraising page for an organisation at all. They can start a campaign (title, description, dates and a goal, checked field by field), change it, pause and resume it, and end it after a warning page that offers a pause instead. Each campaign has a page with what has been raised, passed on and is still held; each hand-over from the community, with Confirm received while it waits; the gifts (donor contact and Gift Aid details are never shown); and the full history. A part of that page that fails to load says so without hiding the rest. New strings in all eleven languages (govuk_alpha_volunteering.org_fundraising.*), reusing the website's wording; Stripe (a brand name, every language) and Cheque (Spanish, Dutch, Portuguese) and Platform (Dutch) are added to scripts/php-lang-invariant-allowlist.json as words a translator would leave alone.

  • Volunteering → organisation dashboard (accessible site): Volunteer qualifications, where an organisation's owner and administrators confirm their volunteers' qualifications, as on the website since 5 Oct 2026. Until now nobody could confirm a qualification on the accessible site. (A volunteer still records their own qualifications on the website: the accessible site has no page for that yet, only the older document-upload page, which is no longer linked.) The register shows what needs attention first (awaiting confirmation or expiring soon), with counts, a search, and Confirmed, Expired and All views. Confirm asks how it was checked (saw the original, checked an online register, or the issuer confirmed it); nothing is uploaded or stored. Withdraw asks for a reason. No one can confirm their own qualification, and an expired one must have its expiry date updated by the volunteer first; both refusals come back in plain words. New strings in all eleven languages (govuk_alpha_volunteering.org_qualifications.*), reusing the website's wording, rewritten to the formal "you" in Spanish and Dutch as the rest of the accessible site is.

  • Volunteering → organisation dashboard: a new Opportunities tab lists everything the organisation has posted: open, closed to new volunteers, and cancelled (the public list shows only open ones). Each shows how many applications are waiting for a decision, how many volunteers are approved and how many shifts are coming up, with Manage, Edit and Post opportunity links. Before, an organiser had to browse the public list to find their own opportunities, and could not find closed or cancelled ones at all. New route GET /v2/volunteering/organisations/{id}/opportunities, open to the same people as the rest of the dashboard.

  • Volunteering → an opportunity's Shifts panel (organisers) and Admin → Volunteering → Opportunities & shifts: an Ask for help button on every upcoming shift sends an urgent request to the volunteers already approved for that opportunity who are not on the shift (up to 50; optionally only those listing a named skill). The organiser chooses how urgent it is and how long to keep asking, and is told how many volunteers were asked. Active requests are listed above the shifts, with how many were asked, accepted and declined, and can be withdrawn. Before, nothing on any screen could send one, so the volunteers' Alerts tab could never fill. New route GET /v2/volunteering/opportunities/{id}/emergency-alerts, for the people who may manage the opportunity. POST /v2/volunteering/emergency-alerts now returns notified.

  • Volunteering → an opportunity's page: the people who manage it (its creator, the organisation's owner and admins, community admins) now get Edit, Close to new volunteers / Reopen and Cancel opportunity, and Edit opens a pre-filled form at /volunteering/opportunities/{id}/edit. Before, the website could not edit, close or cancel an opportunity at all. Closing takes it off the volunteering list and refuses new applications, while the volunteers already on it keep their places. Cancelling asks first, removes it for good and tells approved volunteers. The page's badge now reads Cancelled for a cancelled opportunity, where it used to say "Closed". PUT /v2/volunteering/opportunities/{id} accepts status (open or closed); any other value gets 422.

  • Volunteering → an opportunity's Shifts panel (organisers) and Admin → Volunteering → Opportunities & shifts: every shift now has a Who's coming button listing the volunteers on it by name, each marked as coming, checked in (with the time), checked out or did not come; the groups that booked places, with who booked and which members are confirmed; and the waitlist in order. Before, an organiser saw only "1 of 2 places taken", and attendance appeared on no screen. New route GET /v2/volunteering/shifts/{id}/roster, open only to people who may manage the opportunity (its creator, the organisation's owner and admins, community admins).

  • Volunteering → Organisations and admins can now create, change and remove shifts. Until today nothing on the platform could create a shift: the only server route was a repeating-pattern endpoint that no screen called, and a one-off shift had no route at all, so every feature built on shifts (sign-up, waitlists, group sign-ups, check-in, reminders, swaps) was unreachable for a real organisation. An opportunity's page now carries a Shifts panel for whoever may manage it (the person who posted it, the owning organisation's owner or admins, and community admins), with Add a shift (date, start, end, optional number of places), Add repeating shifts (every day, week, two weeks or month, on chosen weekdays, with an optional last date or maximum count), Edit and Remove on any shift that has not started, and Stop repeating on a pattern. Repeating shifts are created 14 days ahead the moment the pattern is saved, and the existing nightly job keeps topping them up. Removing a shift keeps every volunteer's application to the opportunity, clears their place on that shift, and tells them by bell notification in their own language. A shift cannot be removed or changed once it has started, cannot end before it starts, and cannot be shrunk below the number of volunteers already on it. The admin panel gains Volunteering → Opportunities & shifts, listing every opportunity in the community with the same panel under each. New API: POST /v2/volunteering/opportunities/{id}/shifts, PUT /v2/volunteering/shifts/{id}, DELETE /v2/volunteering/shifts/{id}; the shift list now includes recurring_pattern_id; creating a repeating pattern returns shifts_generated. All new wording is in all eleven languages. The accessible site does not offer shift management yet.

  • Volunteering → Volunteers can now ask to swap a shift on the website. Since 24 August the phone app could ask for a swap, but the website could only answer one, and the Swap Requests tab's own empty state pointed members at a "shift details page" control that had never been built. On My Applications, every confirmed shift that has not started yet now carries an Ask to swap button. It opens a picker of the other future shifts on the same opportunity that have someone on them (the number signed up per shift was already public), and the member picks the shift they would rather do. The platform asks whoever holds that shift without revealing their name, exactly as the app does; the other volunteer accepts or rejects from their own Swap Requests tab, and where the community requires it an admin approves last. A request that gets no response is retried once under the same key, so a dropped connection cannot create two requests. The tab's empty-state wording now points at My Applications, in all eleven languages. The accessible site's swap form, which still asks for a typed shift number and the other person's user ID, is unchanged and remains unusable in practice.

  • Volunteering → Fundraising alerts. Four things that used to happen silently now send a bell notification and an email, each in the recipient's own language: (1) when an organisation starts a fundraising campaign from its own dashboard, the community's admins are told it is already live, with a Review or pause this campaign button that opens the admin page with that campaign's pause confirmation (nothing is paused until the admin confirms); (2) when a community admin pauses or ends an organisation's campaign, the organisation's owners and admins are told; (3) when an organisation confirms it received money the community passed on, the community's admins are told; (4) when a gift to an organisation's campaign is received (a card payment succeeds, or an admin marks a pledge as paid), the organisation's owners and admins are told, with the donor's name or "a donor who asked to stay anonymous", never an email address. The person who made the change is not emailed about it. A failed alert is logged and never undoes the change or fails a Stripe payment confirmation.

  • Volunteer expenses — volunteers now hear about every decision in the app as well as by email. Approval, rejection and payment of a claim each send an in-app notification and a phone push (vol_expense_reviewed, vol_expense_paid) alongside the existing email, in the volunteer's own language.

  • Volunteer expenses — a claim can name the opportunity it was for. The claim forms on the website and the accessible site offer an optional "Opportunity" choice listing only the opportunities the volunteer was accepted onto at the chosen organisation (the API already accepted opportunity_id; no form offered it). On the accessible site, which works without JavaScript, it is one list grouped by organisation, and choosing an opportunity from a different organisation is refused with a message that names the field. The phone app does not offer it yet.

  • Footer "Powered by" badge for a whole network of communities. Admin → Settings → Powered-by branding (platform owner only) now has a second box, "Badge for communities under this one". Fill it in once on a hub community (for example Timebanking UK) and every community under it, at any depth and including communities created later, shows that badge — label, link and image — instead of the Project NEXUS one. The hub's own footer keeps its own badge (the Project NEXUS default unless set). A community that sets its own badge uses only its own: the image, label and link are never mixed from two sources. Both badges also get a wording choice: "Powered by" (the default), "Provided by", or custom text. The first two are shown in each member's own language; custom text is shown as typed and is not translated. Applies to the web app and the accessible site. New settings general.network_powered_by_{wording,label,url,image_light,image_dark} and general.powered_by_wording; new API POST /v2/admin/settings/network-powered-by-image-light|dark. Saving or uploading a network badge refreshes every community under the hub at once. All new wording is in all eleven languages.

  • Help & support → Jira: every ticket the platform raises in the help desk can now also be watched by other support staff, so Jira emails them about it as well as the person it is assigned to. The help desk's own notification setting only emails a ticket's assignee, watchers and reporter, so a second agent heard nothing. New server setting SUPPORT_JIRA_WATCHER_ACCOUNT_IDS (comma-separated Atlassian account ids; empty = no watchers). A failed watcher keeps the ticket and is recorded on the report, like a failed assignment. Covers tickets raised through the platform only, not ones sent to the help desk by email or through its portal.

  • Every volunteering safeguarding incident now has a case record — a permanent history (who did what and when, which nobody can edit or delete; the database refuses it) and a page for each kind of person involved. Staff (admin panel /admin/volunteering/safeguarding/:id, broker panel /broker/safeguarding/volunteering/:id) get a case file: the report, the status with a required reason for resolving, escalating or closing, the handler, how it is filed, the authorities told, team notes, messages to the reporter or the organisation, sharing the full report with the organisation's safeguarding lead, and the whole history with filters. The incident list opens each case, can show only incidents nobody is handling yet, and its figure tiles filter by status; the old update dialog and its "Recent actions" card (which listed incidents, not actions) are gone. The person who reported it gets a page in the web app and on the accessible site (/volunteering/incidents/:id) with its reference, a plain-words status ("Being looked into", "Passed to a specialist"…), what has happened since, messages from the team, and a box to add information until it is closed; the report form now ends with the reference and a link to that page. The organisation it is linked to — its owner, administrators and safeguarding lead/deputy — gets a Safeguarding reports page (/volunteering/org/:orgId/safeguarding, a tab on the organisation dashboard, and /volunteering/organisations/:id/safeguarding on the accessible site) showing a summary of each report, the team's messages and a box to send the team an update; the lead sees the full report only while staff share it, and nobody in the organisation is ever shown who made a report. Each person is told by bell and email what they need to know, in their own language, with no written text in any email; nobody is told about an incident about themselves. New API: GET /v2/admin/volunteering/incidents/{id}, POST …/notes, POST …/messages, POST|DELETE …/share; GET /v2/volunteering/incidents/{id} (the reporter's view) and POST …/additions; GET /v2/volunteering/organisations/{orgId}/incidents, GET …/incidents/{id}, POST …/incidents/{id}/updates. Existing incidents keep their old notes as the first entries of their history. All new wording is in all eleven languages.

  • Group exchanges explain themselves, and two new kinds (web app, accessible site and phone app). Starting a group exchange now asks "What kind of group exchange is this?" and offers five kinds, each with a one-sentence explanation and a worked example: Workshop or class (the new default — the person running it earns the hours they put in, everyone attending pays the hours they attended, and any hours left over go to the community's time fund), A team helping someone (each helper earns the hours they spent and the person helped pays for all of it), Share equally, Share by amount of effort and Type each person's hours (the existing three, renamed and explained). The page states the rule "One hour of time is one time credit. People giving time earn credits; people receiving time pay them." and says "Giving time" / "Receiving time" instead of "providers" / "receivers". Before anything is saved, the form shows one plain line per person ("Mary earns 2 hours", "Tom pays 2 hours"), the hours going to the community time fund and the totals, worked out by the server; a split that cannot go ahead is explained in plain words (for example, a workshop whose organisers would earn more than the attendees pay is pointed at "A team helping someone"). Each participant sees "You will earn…" or "You will pay…" before confirming. Completing a workshop credits the leftover hours to the community fund in the same transaction as every balance, conserved to the cent; the fund records them as group_exchange entries and each attendee's wallet shows their share as a payment to the community time fund. API: new POST /v2/group-exchanges/preview; split_type accepts workshop and team; GET /v2/group-exchanges/{id} returns community_fund_hours. All new wording is in every language.

  • Volunteering safeguarding incidents now reach the organisation they are about. When a report is linked to an organisation — by the reporter, or later by staff — its owner, administrators and designated liaison person (and deputy) get a bell and an email saying a report has been linked to it, what kind of report it is, how serious, when it happened and which opportunity. They are deliberately not told who made the report, who it is about or what it says, because a report can be about the organisation itself; the community's safeguarding team has the full record. The reporter, anyone the report is about, and anyone already alerted as community staff are not sent it. Admin → Volunteering → Safeguarding & incidents (and the broker panel's copy) has a new How this incident is filed section in each incident: staff can link, change or remove its organisation and opportunity, correct its type, severity and date, and record that the police or another authority was told, with their reference. Both report forms — the web app and the accessible site — now open with a warning to call the local emergency number if someone is in immediate danger, and say who will be told about the report. The staff alert email now names the organisation, opportunity and date, and gives the kind of incident in words. All new wording is in all eleven languages. API: PUT /v2/admin/volunteering/incidents/{id} accepts organization_id, opportunity_id, incident_type, incident_date, authority_notified and authority_reference, and now validates severity.

  • Volunteering → Fundraising campaigns can raise money for an organisation. When an administrator creates or edits a campaign (Admin → Volunteering → Fundraising campaigns) they can choose which approved volunteering organisation it is for, or leave it for the whole community; the campaign list has an Organisation column. Every donation to that campaign records the organisation on the donation itself (decided by the server from the campaign, never by the donor's browser), so it stays correct even if the campaign is edited later. Card payments now tell Stripe who the gift is for: the payment description reads "Donation to {organisation} via {community} - {campaign}" and the payment carries nexus_beneficiary (organization or community), nexus_organization_id, nexus_organization_name, nexus_giving_day_id and nexus_giving_day_title, so the finance team can reconcile a payout in Stripe without opening the platform. The money still goes to the community's own Stripe account — this labels the gift, it does not send money to the organisation. Members see "For {organisation}" on the campaign card, in My donations and on the receipt, and the card checkout says which organisation the donation supports. The admin donation list and CSV export include the organisation and can be filtered by it. A gift made against a volunteering opportunity is credited to that opportunity's organisation.

  • Volunteering → Safeguarding → Report an incident (web app): the form now asks what kind of incident it is (a welfare concern, an allegation, something someone disclosed, a near miss, or something else), when it happened, which organisation and volunteering opportunity it was with, and which member it is about. Every new question is optional except the kind, which starts on "a concern". Before this, every report reached staff with no organisation, opportunity or person, as type "other" and dated the day it was sent. New route GET /v2/volunteering/incidents/report-options lists the community's active organisations and their opportunities, by name only; POST /v2/volunteering/incidents now refuses an incident_date in the future, and a blank date still means today. Admin → Volunteering → Safeguarding & incidents, and the broker panel's copy of it, now show each incident's title, organisation, opportunity and date, plus a Who is handling this? picker. Staff can hand an incident to any active administrator, broker or coordinator, but never to the person it is about, and the new handler gets a notification and an email. The staff list response now includes handlers.

Database triggers refuse any UPDATE or DELETE of that table, and the retention job never prunes it. Community admins see the history in the campaign window (Admin → Volunteering → Fundraising campaigns → View donors → History), with Stripe references; organisations see their own campaigns' history without donor identities.

  • Volunteering → Hand-overs: a record of money passed on to an organisation. A hand-over can never exceed what the campaign still holds; it cannot be edited or deleted (database-enforced), only cancelled with a reason. The organisation's owners and admins get an email, bell and push notification in their own language and confirm receipt from their dashboard. New vol_fundraising_handovers table.

  • Volunteering → Organisations run their own fundraising campaigns. The organisation dashboard has a new Fundraising tab (also reached from the hand-over email) where an approved organisation's owners and admins create, edit, pause, resume and end campaigns for their own organisation — live straight away, no approval step — and see each campaign's gifts (name or "Anonymous"; never email or Gift Aid details), hand-overs and history. Seven new /v2/volunteering/organisations/{id}/... endpoints; the organisation always comes from the URL, never the request body.

  • Donations → Stripe carries the platform donation number. Card checkout now creates the pending donation before the PaymentIntent, so the PaymentIntent metadata includes nexus_donation_id; a webhook that arrives before the intent id is saved is matched by that number. Platform refunds carry nexus_donation_id, nexus_giving_day_id, nexus_organization_id and nexus_refunded_by_user_id. A checkout Stripe refuses to start is kept as a failed donation with a history entry.

Without JavaScript the opportunity list cannot be narrowed to the chosen organisation, so each opportunity is shown with its organisation’s name and a mismatched pair is refused with its own message. If the list of organisations cannot be loaded, the form says so and the report can still be sent. The member’s list of their own reports gains an Organisation column, and the form is no longer shown filled in again after a report is sent successfully. All new wording is in all eleven languages.

A nightly job marks records expired on the date and sends an "expiring soon" reminder (window from the existing admin reminder setting, now called Qualification expiry, default 30 days) and an "expired" notice to the volunteer by email and bell, plus a digest to the owner and admins of each organisation the volunteer is linked to. API: GET/POST /v2/volunteering/qualifications, PUT /v2/volunteering/qualifications/{id}, POST …/{id}/withdraw, POST …/{id}/confirm, GET /v2/volunteering/organizations/{id}/qualifications, GET /v2/admin/volunteering/qualifications; command volunteering:qualification-expiry. The old upload endpoints and table are untouched for now (no production uploads existed); their removal is a separate step.

The member types a name and presses Find member; the page comes back with the matching members of the community to choose from, and everything already typed is kept. It works without JavaScript, the name searched for is never put in the page address (so it does not end up in browser history or server logs), the reporter is never offered as the person, and a name typed but never looked up is refused with a message rather than silently dropped. Pressing Enter in any box still sends the report rather than running a search. Staff see the chosen member under "Subject", exactly as for reports from the web app. All new wording is in all eleven languages.

  • Admin → CRM → CRM overview (the CRM front page): it now opens with a Needs a coordinator strip listing what is waiting right now — overdue tasks, tasks due today and members waiting for approval — each a link into the list with that filter applied, or a green "Nothing is waiting on you" when all three are zero. The eight figures (members, active in the last 30 days, new this month, waiting for approval, open tasks, overdue tasks, member notes, tags in use) each carry a plain-English hint (never signed in, share of members active, assigned to you, added in the last 30 days, members with a tag) and each links to the page it comes from. Two new cards show Your next tasks — the open tasks assigned to you, overdue first, with an Overdue / Due today / due-date marker and the member each is about — and Recent notes, the latest notes coordinators have written, with the member (linking to their notes), category, pin and author; concern notes the reader may not see are left out, exactly as on the notes page. The five CRM tools plus the member list are a row of cards, each with a one-line description. One Export menu replaces three buttons and offers the overview figures, notes, tasks, tags and activity CSVs; the overview CSV now carries every figure on the page (it had five of thirteen). A line says when the figures were loaded, a failed load shows an error with Retry, refreshing keeps the figures on screen instead of blanking them, and the page keeps to the screen on a phone. API: GET /v2/admin/crm/dashboard additionally returns tasks_due_today, my_tasks, next_tasks, notes_last_30_days, recent_notes, tags_in_use and tagged_members.

  • Volunteering → Donations tab rebuilt. Fundraising campaigns are now grouped into Live campaigns (with the donate buttons), Coming up and Past campaigns (closed, no buttons), and each card says how much has been raised of the goal in the community's currency, the percentage funded, the number of donors and when it ends ("Ends 23 October 2026 · in 18 days"). Three summary tiles show live campaigns, the money raised across them, and what you have given (completed gifts, with a note of any pledge still pending) — replacing a "Total donors" figure that double-counted anyone who gave to two campaigns. My donations names the campaign on each gift, says "Card", "Bank transfer", "PayPal" or "Cash", explains on a pending pledge that an administrator confirms it when the money arrives, and offers View receipt on completed card gifts. The pledge form picks the campaign (or general support), shows the currency next to the amount, offers bank transfer, PayPal or cash only (card payments have the real checkout), and takes an optional payment reference so the administrator can match the transfer. A failed load shows an error with Try again, and refreshing keeps the figures on screen instead of blanking them. API: GET /v2/volunteering/donations returns giving_day_title on each row.

  • Admin → CRM → Onboarding funnel: the page can now be narrowed to a cohort — members who joined in the last 30 days, 90 days or 12 months, or everyone — so a coordinator can see whether recent recruits are getting through; the cohort and the step whose list is open live in the address (?joined=90&step=email_verified), so a reload, the back button or a shared link lands on the same view. Each waiting member now shows how long ago they joined ("3 weeks ago") beside the date. The member, activity type, date range and page live in the address (?user_id=&type=&days=&page=), so a reload, the back button or a link from a member's page lands on the same view. The date range is a row of buttons (7 / 30 / 90 days / all time), the type filter has an explicit All types choice, each row has a show only this member button, the empty view offers Show all time or Clear filters, a failed load shows an error with Retry instead of "No activity found", and refreshing or changing a filter keeps the list on screen instead of blanking the page. An Export activity button downloads a CSV of the current view (new GET /v2/admin/crm/export/timeline, admin only, same filters, capped at 5,000 rows).

Adding a tag offers the existing tags first (with their counts) so one idea does not end up spelled three ways, says when a member already has the tag instead of a generic failure, and pre-fills the tag when adding from a tag's members view. Removing asks for confirmation naming the tag and the member (or the number of members), and an Export tags button downloads a CSV of every tag assignment grouped by tag.   • Admin → CRM → Coordinator tasks: the page opens on the tasks that still need doing (pending and in progress) instead of everything ever created, with Overdue, each status, and All one click away; a filter by assignee (anyone, you, or a colleague); an Export tasks CSV button; and a results line that says how many tasks match.   • A script, scripts/cloudflare-strip-x-powered-by.mjs, that ensures every Cloudflare zone on the account removes the X-Powered-By response header at the edge (the Plesk/Apache origin adds X-Powered-By: PleskLin and has no clean server-wide switch on this setup). Needs a Cloudflare token with Zone:Read + Transform Rules:Edit in CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN or .secrets.local/cloudflare-transform-token. Removes the low-severity header-disclosure item O-181 (security register E-089).

Four headline cards (Members, Active listings, Exchanges this month, Hours exchanged this month) carry the change against last month; a second row shows members active in the last 30 days, new members this month, total listings and all-time hours. An Exchange activity chart replaces the text rows: hours exchanged and number of exchanges by month for the last twelve months. Reached from the dashboard, a new My listings entry in the Timebanking menu, and a button on the Listings page. The Archive export carries every column of the record.

Monitoring: a search box, All / Messaging off / Expiring soon tabs, an Extend action and a Refresh button. Risk tags: ?listing=<id> opens the tag form for that listing; listing titles link to the listing. Configuration: a sticky save bar with Discard, a warning before leaving with unsaved changes, number fields that show their unit, and section jump links.

Translated into all seven app languages. No new native code, so it can ship as an over-the-air update — but only after a store build that includes the earlier expo-updates 55.0.33 patch, which already blocks an over-the-air update of main.

Available in all eleven languages.

  • Broker dashboard: a "Waiting for you" section lists the first few items of each queue — new members, unreviewed messages, exchanges needing action, member reports — with the quick decisions right there: Approve a new member (after the same confirmation the Members page asks) and Mark reviewed a routine message. New route POST /v2/admin/broker/messages/review-bulk (broker or admin, at most 50, 30 per minute). Each message keeps the single-review rules — another community's copy is not found, the broker's own conversation is refused — and is audited on its own, marked as bulk. On the Messages list the message preview now opens the message too (only the sender's name did).

New route POST /v2/admin/broker/exchanges/{id}/cancel-dispute (broker or admin, refuses a party to the exchange, reason required). The broker Help Centre guide "What can I do when an exchange goes wrong?" is rewritten in all 11 languages.

  • Broker panel: a completed exchange whose credits moved can be reversed from its page with Reverse exchange and a reason. This uses the existing reversal (a correcting entry beside the original; the server's party and rank checks are unchanged). A reversed exchange says so.

  • Broker dashboard: two new cards, New members to approve and Member reports to check, and "What needs you now" lists every waiting queue instead of the first four. Each card's number is counted by the same rule as the list it opens, with a test that compares the two. The broker sidebar gains a count on Reports, and Members now takes its count from the dashboard.

  • Support reports can now be copied to the Jira Service Management help desk, so they can be answered there. The connection is switched off by default (SUPPORT_JIRA_ENABLED). It connects as an Atlassian service account, which does not use a help-desk agent seat. Its scoped API token works only through the Atlassian platform gateway, so SUPPORT_JIRA_CLOUD_ID sends API calls there, while SUPPORT_JIRA_SITE_URL is used for the admins' "Open in Jira" links. All settings are documented in .env.example. A new command, php artisan support:jira-check, proves the connection works while it is still switched off. It checks the key, the help desk and the four request types, and changes nothing. With --create-test-ticket it raises one ticket marked TEST, using the same steps as a real report, and stores nothing on the platform. When the connection is on, every saved report creates a ticket in the background. A Jira outage never loses a report or slows the member down. The ticket carries the reference, community, platform user id, page path, app version, Sentry link and impact (as a priority), and the technical details come as an attached file. It never includes the member's IP hash. By default the ticket is raised under the platform's service account with no member name or email. A second switch, SUPPORT_JIRA_SEND_MEMBER_EMAIL (also off), raises it in the member's name so Jira can email them replies. The admin support-reports view shows the Jira ticket and any sync error. Every 15 minutes the platform reads each ticket's status back from Jira (support:jira-sync-status; read only, it never writes to Jira and needs no Atlassian setting changed). A ticket that is done in Jira marks the report resolved, and a reopened one moves it back to triaged. A report linked to Jira shows its Jira status. Its status can't be changed by hand any more (422 SUPPORT_REPORT_HANDLED_IN_JIRA), but it can still be closed and given notes. On the website, the "Report a problem" button is now Help & support. Members first choose what they need: something isn't working, how do I…?, an account or sign-in problem, or a suggestion. Only "something isn't working" asks how badly it affects them and offers to attach technical details. After sending, the form shows just the confirmation and its reference, and the member is emailed a receipt in their own language. The receipt gives the reference, the type of request and the summary, and never includes technical details. The platform sends it itself, whatever the Jira switches say. If the receipt fails, the request still goes through (SupportReportNotificationService::sendReceipt). The platform receipt is always sent, even when Jira will email the member too: it goes out through the platform's own authenticated domain and reaches the inbox, whereas Jira's first message to a new customer (a "confirm your email address" request from a *.atlassian.net address) was seen landing in junk, and Jira holds every later notification until it is clicked. When Jira will also write, the receipt names Jira's sender address (SUPPORT_JIRA_NOTIFICATION_SENDER, default jira@<site>) and tells the member to look in their junk folder for that confirmation. With that switch on, the ticket is raised in the member's name and its description also names them and gives their email address. The ticket is raised directly in the member's email address and Jira creates the help-desk customer itself (Atlassian's separate "create customer" call needs a Jira administrator, which the platform's account deliberately is not). If Jira refuses to raise it in the member's name, the ticket is raised under the platform's account with the member's details in it, the refusal is shown on the admin page, and the member gets the platform's own receipt email instead. Every failed attempt is now shown on the admin page, not only the ones Jira answered. A new setting, SUPPORT_JIRA_ASSIGNEE_ACCOUNT_ID, assigns every new ticket to the person who answers the help desk, so Jira emails them. The admin support-reports page shows each report's type, its Jira ticket and status, an "Open in Jira" link and any Jira error. A report handled in Jira can only keep its status or be closed there. The member and admin Help Centre guides are updated to match, in all 11 languages. Reports now carry a request type (broken, how_to, account, suggestion; default broken): only broken asks for an impact and keeps diagnostics. Each member may send at most 5 reports in any 24 hours (429 SUPPORT_REPORT_DAILY_LIMIT).

Fixed

  • Members — the background map lookup for members' towns can no longer get stuck on towns it cannot find. Every 30 minutes the platform looked up the map position of up to 50 members per community who had a town but no position, with no ordering and no record of having tried. A community with 50 towns the map service could not find was asked about the same 50 on every run, and nobody after them was ever looked up; a large member import would have made this much worse. A new command, members:geocode-pending (every minute, all communities, up to 10 members and about 12 seconds per run so it does not hold up the other scheduled jobs, one request a second as the map service requires), marks each member as attempted before asking, takes never-tried members first and then the longest-ago attempts, and asks about an unfound town again only after 7 days, or at once if the member (or an admin) changes their town. The 30-minute job still looks up listings but no longer members; the manual /cron/geocode-batch page uses the same safe lookup, capped at 20 members and about 20 seconds because it runs inside a web request. A map-service failure (too many requests, a server error, a timeout) is treated differently from "town not found": those members are asked again in about an hour rather than a week, and the run stops after three such failures in a row, so a short outage cannot park hundreds of members. Uses the new users.geocode_attempted_at column (migration 2026_10_09_100100). Because users has a full-text search index, adding it is not instant: MariaDB rebuilds users, and writes to it wait until that finishes (about 2.5 seconds for 63,000 rows in a local test), so check the production row count before deploying.

  • Infrastructure — a full Redis no longer silently deletes queued jobs and locks. Production Redis (nexus-php-redis), which holds the queue including delayed jobs, Horizon's records, the cache and every lock, ran maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru. When full, that deletes any key without an error. The policy had been changed to volatile-lru in the old compose.prod.yml on 2026-05-02, but the container (created 2026-05-01) was never recreated, and that file was deleted on 2026-08-09. That left production Redis with no definition in the repository. It is now defined in compose.redis.yml with noeviction, so a full Redis refuses writes loudly instead. The 400 MB data limit is unchanged, and the container memory ceiling rises from 512M to 768M to leave room for Redis rewriting its save file. Local compose.yml and compose.ci.yml use the same policy. Every deploy now re-asserts the policy and logs usage and evictions (secure_redis_eviction_policy), and stops only if the policy cannot be set. Measured before the change on 2026-10-09: 3.8 MB peak in 7.9 days, 0 keys evicted. The policy was switched live on production the same day, which does not survive a Redis restart until the container is recreated from the new file. Regression test: scripts/test/test-redis-eviction-policy.sh.

  • Registration — the welcome email no longer splits the surrounding database transaction. SendWelcomeNotification ran CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS email_verification_tokens every time someone registered. MariaDB commits any open transaction before a table-creation statement, even when the table already exists, so work that should have been all-or-nothing around a registration could be half-saved. In tests it ended each test's automatic rollback, so one registration test's community settings stayed in the test database and made another test fail when the two ran side by side. The listener now checks Schema::hasTable() first and only creates the table if it is genuinely missing (it is part of the normal schema). Regression test: tests/Laravel/Feature/Listeners/SendWelcomeNotificationTransactionTest.php. The recovery command emails:resend-stuck-activations (ResendStuckVerificationEmails) had the same unconditional create and now has the same check; its own tests had been leaving their seeded test communities, members and verification links in the test database.

The rebuilt import shows every count, and the phone numbers and negative numbers that the platform's own export writes with a leading apostrophe now come back in without it.

Security

  • F-577 (Low): per-member rate limits on signed-in routes counted by network address instead. On every authenticated API route the throttle: middleware runs before App\Http\Middleware\Authenticate (that class is not in Laravel's middleware priority list), so when a named limiter ran, $request->user() was always null for a bearer-token caller and the limiter fell back to its per-address key. Affected: every nexus-route-* tier on a signed-in route (about 194 routes), the groups-* family, bulk-export, events-people-bulk, podcast-media, and the signed-in branch of mfa-challenge. Members sharing one address (an office, a care home, a mobile carrier's shared address) shared each other's allowance, and one member changing address got a fresh one. The group-wide api limiter was already correct (F-036). Every limiter now takes the member from a verified access token, the way F-036 does, through one helper, RouteServiceProvider::verifiedActorId(); unverified, expired or revoked bearer text still counts by address. RouteThrottleIdentityTest sweeps the live router so a new limiter on a signed-in route is covered automatically. The member-import limiters stay per-address on purpose; their per-administrator limit is enforced in the controller.

  • F-572 (Low): confirming an email could make an account held for its identity check look live. An account an administrator creates on a community that requires an identity check is stored approved but pending until the check passes (F-278). Confirming the email activated any approved, pending account, so a held member who asked the public "resend verification" form for a link and clicked it became active — visible to member search, digests and other "live member" lists — while the check was still outstanding. They still could not sign in. Confirming an email now never activates an account whose identity check is unfinished or refused, on every path. Regression test: EmailVerificationControllerTest::test_verify_email_does_not_release_an_account_held_for_its_identity_check.

  • Volunteering — nobody can confirm their own shift check-in or check-out. A volunteer who was also on the organisation's team (or a community admin) could scan-verify their own check-in code and check themselves out, attesting their own attendance. The server now refuses that with a clear message; another organiser has to do it.

  • Feed posts and group discussions now keep only the formatting their editors can make (F-569, follow-up to Cyphere's stored-HTML-injection finding). The feed post editor makes bold, italic, underline, strike, lists and links; the group discussion editor also makes two heading sizes and quotes. Anything else — a large heading, a picture loaded from another site, a table — could only reach a post by being sent straight to the API, and it then showed on the page. It is now removed both before saving and when showing the post; the words inside it are kept. Links show only their real address as the clickable part, and this is now also enforced before saving: a member's own link words are stored as plain text followed by the full address as the only link (fake "user@" prefixes removed, look-alike international domain names stored in their encoded form), so the saved post and every API response match what the page shows. No existing post, discussion or help answer on production used any of the removed formatting, so nothing anyone can see today changes.

  • Typed HTML in a comment or description is now shown as plain text, never rendered (F-568; root cause behind Cyphere's F-562 stored-HTML-injection retest). Comments and the description boxes for listings, events, groups, ideas and job adverts are plain typing boxes with no formatting buttons, yet whatever was typed into them used to be treated as web code when shown back: a member could type a heading, a table, an image pulled from any website, or a link, and it rendered. The earlier F-562 fix only stopped the link text being clickable, so every other tag still rendered. Now these boxes store and show exactly what was typed, as words — any HTML tag appears as plain text, the same way the accessible site and the phone app already behave. This covers comments everywhere (feed, events, polls, listings), the listing/event/group/idea/job descriptions, and group announcements, questions and answers, and challenges. Genuinely formatted areas that are meant to have formatting (feed posts, group discussions) and all staff-written content (blog, knowledge base, legal, custom pages) are unchanged. Server side, the same text-only rule is applied before storage, so the protection does not depend on the browser.

The dependency audit that blocks the Security Scan passes again; nothing in the installed app changes.

  • A member's own words can no longer be a link (F-562, Cyphere retest of 6 Oct 2026). The 4 Oct fix kept a member's link clickable and showed its destination beside it; Cyphere retested and failed it, because the words the member chose were still the link. Now, in anything a member writes (listing, event, group and organisation descriptions, posts, comments), every link is unwrapped: the member's words stay as plain text and are followed by one link whose text is its own address, written out in full with any fake user-name part removed and look-alike international names shown in punycode. A link whose text already is its address (a pasted URL) is left alone. Administrator content (blog, knowledge base, legal, custom pages) is unchanged. The accessible site and the phone app never rendered member links as live. The address link is shown as a link (underlined, in the platform colour) and wraps inside a narrow comment box instead of overflowing it; and if the page ever has no document to work with, the link tags are dropped and the words kept rather than letting a labelled link through.

  • Volunteering: a person allowed to decide an opportunity's applications (for example an organisation admin) could approve their own application to it. Nobody can decide their own application now, whatever their role; PUT /v2/volunteering/applications/{id} answers 403.

  • Dependency security fixes (accessible site and phone app). proxy-addr 2.0.7 → 2.0.8 in the accessible site (CVE-2026-90711, rated critical; Express uses it to work out each visitor's address behind the proxy) and source-map-js 1.2.1 → 1.2.2 in the accessible site and the phone app's build tools (CVE-2026-93749 / GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q, a denial of service from a malformed source map). Version bumps only, within the ranges Express, PostCSS, Sass and Tailwind already accept; nothing else changes.

  • The footer "Powered by" badge settings are now platform-owner only on the server, not just in the admin screen. The badge's label and link could be changed by any community admin with a direct PUT /v2/admin/settings request; the admin screen hid the fields but the server did not check. Every badge setting now needs users.is_god, the same rule the badge image uploads already had. Badge links must be full http:// or https:// addresses, and a badge image can only be set by uploading a file (the settings request may only clear one).

  • Volunteering safeguarding: when an incident was reported about a member of community staff, that staff member was sent the same alert as everyone else — bell and email, with the title and the reporter's name. Nobody is now told about an incident that is about them, matching the existing rule that nobody sees or handles such an incident (F-507).

  • The member wallet statement CSV uses the shared formula guard (F-565, Low; E-089). GET /v2/wallet/statement (also behind the accessible frontend's wallet export) neutralised spreadsheet formulas with its own rule that looked only at the first character, so a trigger behind leading whitespace or a control character (" =1+1", "\x01+1+1") passed through. Every CSV the platform writes now goes through CsvExportSanitizer. Found while re-auditing Cyphere's wallet CSV finding (F-561); not reported by Cyphere and not shown to be exploitable in Excel.

  • Members can no longer hide transfers from their own wallet history (F-564, Informational; E-089, Cyphere pen test). DELETE /v2/wallet/transactions/{id} set a per-member hide flag on a transfer. The balance and the other party's record were never touched and no client offered the action, but a member must not be able to edit their own view of the time-credit ledger. The route, controller action and service method are removed; hide flags already set are still honoured on read, and nothing can set new ones.

  • Links in member-written text now show where they really go (F-562, Medium; E-089, Cyphere pen test). A member could put <a href="https://evil.example/login">Click here to re-authenticate</a> into a listing, event or poll comment and it rendered as an ordinary platform link — safe from script, but a ready-made phishing lure in other members' feeds. sanitizeMemberRichText now appends the destination host (or mailbox) in brackets to every link that leaves the platform's origin unless the visible text already names it, and a link with no text shows its full address. Applied to the sanitiser's output rather than inside a DOMPurify hook, so content removed later cannot satisfy the check. Relative and same-origin links, and administrator-authored content, are unchanged.

  • Spreadsheet exports built in the browser now neutralise formulas, and so does the platform billing export (F-561, Low; E-088). Seven admin and member exports wrote other people's text straight into CSV: Wallet → Export (other members' names and transfer descriptions), Newsletter subscribers (names typed into public sign-up forms), Federation activity, the FADP processing-register export, the Federation and platform audit logs, and Cron job logs. A value such as =HYPERLINK(…) became a live formula when the file was opened in Excel or LibreOffice. A shared react-frontend/src/lib/csv.ts now quotes and neutralises every cell with the same rule as the server's CsvExportSanitizer, and all seven use it. The super-admin billing CSV (TenantBillingService::exportCsv) wrote community and plan names unneutralised — a community's own admin sets its name — and now uses CsvExportSanitizer. Also fixed in passing: the cron log export never doubled inner quotes (a " broke the file), and the platform audit log export put the target and target-type columns under each other's headings.

  • Office uploads must be real Office documents (F-559, Low; E-088). Message attachments, resources and job CVs accepted any ZIP archive as a .docx/.xlsx (a plain archive renamed .docx was accepted at all three). A shared OfficeDocumentInspector now requires a genuine package ([Content_Types].xml plus the main word/, xl/ or ppt/ parts) at all four Office upload points including group files, and refuses packages carrying a macro project (vbaProject.bin or a macro-enabled content type). Group files previously inspected only files the type detector reported as a bare ZIP, so a macro-carrying .docx that it recognised as Word was accepted; it is now inspected too. Legacy .doc/.xls (OLE) files are not inspected.

  • Paper onboarding stores scans under an extension that matches their content (F-560, Low; E-088). PaperOnboardingIntakeService::createFromUpload() kept the extension the uploader sent, so JPEG bytes named x.php were stored as <uuid>.php (private disk, no serving route, admin-only — harmless today, but the exact precondition F-554 guards against). The extension now comes from the detected type (PDF, JPEG, PNG, WebP) and anything else is refused.

  • Admin member CSV import checks the file itself and has limits (F-558, Low; E-088). POST /v2/admin/users/import decided "is this a CSV?" from the type the browser declared — PNG bytes declared text/csv were accepted — and had no size or row limit (a 50,000-row file was processed in one request). The type is now detected from the file's content (text only, no NUL bytes), files over 2 MB are refused, and a file with more than 5,000 rows is refused whole before any account is created. Both new messages are translated in all eleven languages.

  • The admin per-member statement download is a real CSV with formulas neutralised (F-557, Low; E-088). Admin → Timebanking → User report → download built its CSV by joining strings, so a transfer description such as =HYPERLINK(…) was written as a live spreadsheet formula, and it returned the CSV inside a JSON envelope, so the saved .csv file actually contained JSON. It now streams text/csv as an attachment, every cell goes through CsvExportSanitizer, and amounts are signed numbers. The "Balance After" column, which repeated today's balance on every row, is replaced by each transaction's status: balances also change through grants and adjustments that are not in this list, so a per-row balance cannot be computed from it.

  • Knowledge-base attachments are stored privately (F-556, Low; E-088). They were written to the public disk, so a draft article's attachment answered an anonymous request at its /storage/tenant_X/kb_attachments/… address even though the API download route correctly refused members. New uploads (and kb:import) now go to the private disk and are read only through the API route; files already on the public disk still download through the API, and both Apache layers (httpdocs/.htaccess for dev, docker/apache/storage-alias.conf for production) refuse the static kb_attachments path. Retested locally and on the production image.

  • Private file downloads keep their own locked-down Content-Security-Policy (F-555, Low; E-088). Message attachments, voice messages and admin support screenshots send default-src 'none' (with sandbox for message media) so that a stored file opened directly can run nothing, but the platform SecurityHeaders middleware replaced it with the page policy on every API response. It now keeps an endpoint's policy when that policy grants nothing at all (default-src 'none', every other directive 'none' or a bare sandbox) and still replaces anything looser. Verified live on the attachment and screenshot routes.

  • Public storage (/storage) in the production images now gets the same protection as /uploads (F-554, Medium; found by internal review E-088). Production maps /storage to storage/app/public with an Apache Alias outside the web root, so httpdocs/.htaccess — its script-extension guard and its sandbox CSP — never applied there; on the image built from Dockerfile.bluegreen a .php file placed on the public disk ran, and every other file was served with no X-Content-Type-Options and no CSP. No upload path was found that lets a member choose the stored extension, so this was a missing second line of defence rather than a demonstrated exploit. Both images now install one shared docker/apache/storage-alias.conf that refuses script-like files, switches the PHP engine off, and sends nosniff plus the same sandbox CSP as /uploads; retested on the production image (PHP-family files 403, everything else sandboxed). .dockerignore and .gitignore gained the exceptions the new file needs, and a test pins both images, the config and the CSP match.

  • The accessible frontend's error pages named the web framework (F-553, Low; found by an internal review while re-testing F-552). Helmet removes Express's default X-Powered-By header on normal pages, but when the community lookup fails with anything other than "not found" the error is rethrown out of tenantRouting, Express skips every later middleware, and the error page kept X-Powered-By: Express (seen live on /wp-login.php and unknown paths on the accessible hosts). app.disable('x-powered-by') now switches it off at the application level so no response path can send it; a test covers both the normal and the error-page path.

  • Uploaded PDFs could carry JavaScript that ran when another member opened them (F-551, High; reported by Cyphere during the independent penetration test). Cyphere uploaded a PDF with an embedded script to a group's files and confirmed it ran when the file was opened in a browser's PDF viewer. No upload feature looked inside a PDF. A new inspector (app/Support/Uploads/PdfActiveContentInspector.php) reads the PDF's structure, including compressed object streams, objects hidden inside other objects' stream data (a viewer reaches those through the cross-reference table; every obj and trailer keyword is read, so comments or odd spacing in an object's header cannot hide it) and #-escaped names, and refuses scripts, launch actions, form submission, XFA forms and rich media; a file it cannot fully read (an unsupported encoding inside an object stream, a truncated object stream, an encrypted file with object streams, a decompression bomb, or more than 2 seconds of work) is refused rather than passed. Because the check runs before sign-in, one request may cause at most 3 seconds of inspection across all its files. It runs once for every API upload through the new RejectActivePdfUploads middleware in the api group, so messages, group files, team documents, resources, help-centre attachments, job CVs, expense receipts, volunteer credentials and the safeguarding statement are all covered, and GroupFileService repeats the check.
